name: Unrequested Or Partial Changes
problem: A request to change a quest leads to changes that were not asked for, to only part of what was asked, or to the same change made twice.
who_has_it: People and teammates who let the AI edit goals, notes and experiments for them.
why_it_matters: Quest data is the person's own plan. An unrequested write is hard to notice and undo, and a partial change leaves the plan inconsistent while the reply claims success.
why_hard: A change request is natural language mapped onto many tools with many arguments; a model tends to be helpful beyond the ask, multi-step requests need each step done once, and a retry after a timeout can repeat a write.
existing_attempts: Tool schemas with explicit arguments, a confirmation step for destructive actions, a scoped writer that performs only the one named operation, and database-level checks of the final state.

name: Unreadable Outward Text
problem: What an AI writes for people carries machine keys: a record id or a machine-read header line copied from its own instructions into an email subject, a task, a note or an ask.
who_has_it: Readers of autopilot mail and notes (subscribers, teammates, the person who owns the quest) and the person whose name the message goes out under.
why_it_matters: A subject such as 'Quest subscribers: SOLUTIONS YOU ITERATE: esr_b451d0cb3cec' went to real people on 2026-11-16. It says nothing to them, looks broken, and costs trust in everything else the autopilot sends.
why_hard: The machine line sits at the top of the instructions the model must follow, so echoing it looks like obeying; the model also has the ids in hand and not always the names, and a mechanical rewrite of the text cannot know which name belongs to which id.
existing_attempts: A rule in the brief (names, never ids), a title cleaner for batch task titles, and this check at the send boundary, which refuses and names the offending strings so the writer rewrites them.
